title: Fn, FnMut and FnOnce
concept: Capture ownership and how a closure uses its environment

writing.summary: The call trait follows what the closure does with captures, not just whether `move` appears.
writing.explanation:
`Fn` closures can be called through a shared reference, `FnMut` permits a mutable receiver, and `FnOnce` consumes its receiver. The traits form a hierarchy: a closure that implements `Fn` also works where `FnMut` or `FnOnce` is required. Every closure supports at least `FnOnce`, but consuming a captured non-`Copy` value can make a closure callable only once.

The `move` keyword determines how captures enter the closure. It does not alone make the closure `FnOnce`-only. A `move` closure that merely reads owned data may still implement `Fn`. Conversely, mutating captured state generally requires `FnMut`. The example borrows a counter mutably, calls the closure twice, then ends its scope before reading the counter directly.

Read the implementation and the caller’s intended use together. A callback stored for repeated notifications needs a repeated-call contract, while a one-shot cleanup callback can accept `FnOnce`. If the callback crosses a thread or task boundary, `Send` and lifetime bounds are additional questions. In an interview, expect to change only the closure body from reading a `String` to returning the owned `String` and explain which call capability is lost.
writing.exampleCaption: A mutating callback runs twice, while a read-only `move` closure remains repeatedly callable.
writing.rule: `move` controls capture ownership; the closure body determines its call-trait capabilities.
writing.task: Explain the example, predict the result, and justify your answer to the follow-up.
writing.success: Identify the relevant ownership or API contract and test the changed constraint.
writing.question: Why can this `move` closure be called twice?
answers: move makes every captured String implicitly Copy.
The captured String is recreated before every call.
The body reads the owned capture without consuming it.
writing.feedback: The closure owns `text` but only borrows it during each call. Returning `text` by value instead would consume that capture.

depth.misconception: move makes every captured String implicitly Copy.
depth.correction: `String` never becomes `Copy`. `move` transfers the one `String` into the closure, and calls stay repeatable because the body only reads it.
